rows.description: My sibling is pushing hard for a bigger share of family money or land and I feel angry and betrayed. I put agreements in writing, use a neutral elder or lawyer, and avoid cutting the relationship over one dispute if repair is possible.

rows.description: My parents openly favour a sibling in gifts, praise, or the will and I feel unseen and hurt. I say it calmly to them if safe, do not turn it into war with my sibling, and build my worth outside their approval.

rows.description: I feel protective of my younger sibling as they start their life and I want to steer them. I offer support and listen, and I accept that their choices are theirs; controlling them out of love is still control.

rows.description: My sibling turns to me for comfort and honesty as adults and I feel glad and needed. I show up, keep their confidences, and avoid the old roles of bossy elder or spoiled baby that we slid into as children.

rows.description: After our parent's death, my sibling and I grieve differently and misread each other as cold or dramatic. I ask how they are coping, share memories together, and settle assets only after the first wave of grief has passed.

rows.description: I took more than my share of family support and now feel guilty toward my sibling. I acknowledge it honestly and offer fair repair; ignoring it lets silent distance grow, and over-giving to erase guilt helps no one.

rows.description: I am exhausted, sleepless, and afraid I am failing my newborn. Feelings of doubt are common. I ask my partner and family for concrete help, lower my standards for the house, and seek support if the low mood does not lift.

rows.description: I feel a fierce need to shield my baby from every harm. This love is natural; wisdom is to keep the child safe without letting my fear steal their freedom and confidence as they grow.

rows.description: Since the baby arrived my partner and I bicker and feel like co-workers on a rota. I plan short moments to talk, split night duties fairly, and thank them out loud; we protect the relationship the child depends on.
